questions.stem: In the blast furnace, carbon monoxide reduces iron(III) oxide according to: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. What is happening to the carbon monoxide in this reaction?

options.text: It is being reduced because it gains oxygen
It is being oxidised because it gains oxygen to form CO2
It is acting as a catalyst and is unchanged
It is being decomposed into carbon and oxygen

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide gains oxygen (CO -> CO2), so it is oxidised. At the same time, it acts as the reducing agent because it causes the iron(III) oxide to be reduced. The iron oxide loses oxygen and is reduced to iron metal.

questions.stem: A student heats copper oxide with carbon powder in a crucible. She observes the black powder turning brown-pink and a gas is produced that turns limewater milky. What equation represents this reaction?

options.text: CuO + C -> Cu + CO
2CuO + C -> 2Cu + CO2
CuO + C -> CuC + O
CuO + CO2 -> CuCO3

questions.explanation: The black copper oxide (CuO) is reduced to brown-pink copper metal, and the gas that turns limewater milky is carbon dioxide (CO2). The balanced equation is 2CuO + C -> 2Cu + CO2. Carbon reduces the copper oxide by removing the oxygen.

questions.stem: Why can lead oxide be reduced by heating with carbon, but aluminium oxide cannot?

options.text: Lead oxide has a lower melting point than aluminium oxide
Aluminium oxide is a covalent compound that carbon cannot break down
Lead is below carbon in the reactivity series, but aluminium is above carbon
Carbon reacts with aluminium to form a carbide instead

questions.explanation: Carbon can only reduce the oxides of metals that are less reactive than carbon. Lead is below carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon can take the oxygen away from lead oxide. Aluminium is above carbon, meaning aluminium holds onto its oxygen more strongly than carbon can, so reduction with carbon fails.

questions.stem: In the blast furnace, limestone (calcium carbonate) is added along with iron ore and coke. What is the purpose of the limestone?

options.text: It acts as the reducing agent that removes oxygen from iron ore
It provides extra carbon to fuel the furnace
It decomposes to form calcium oxide, which removes sandy impurities as slag
It lowers the melting point of the iron so it flows more easily

questions.explanation: Limestone decomposes in the heat to form calcium oxide (CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2). The calcium oxide then reacts with silicon dioxide (sand) impurities in the ore: CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 (slag). This slag floats on the molten iron and is removed. The coke (carbon) is the reducing agent, not the limestone.

questions.stem: When zinc oxide is heated with carbon, the products are zinc and carbon dioxide. If 8.1 g of zinc oxide reacts completely, approximately how much zinc is produced? (Ar: Zn = 65, O = 16, C = 12)
questions.explanation: The equation is: 2ZnO + C -> 2Zn + CO2. Mr of ZnO = 65 + 16 = 81. Moles of ZnO = 8.1/81 = 0.1 mol. From the equation, 2 mol ZnO produces 2 mol Zn, so 0.1 mol ZnO produces 0.1 mol Zn. Mass of Zn = 0.1 x 65 = 6.5 g.
